newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela May non-oil exports up 41 pct vs yr ago.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela May non-oil exports up 41 pct vs yr ago.

text.p: Venezuela's non-traditional exports, which exclude oil and iron, rose $140 million, or 41.1 percent, at $481 million in May, from $341 million in May 1996, the Central Office of Statistics and Information (OCEI) said Wednesday.
Exports for the first five months of the year, at $1.833 billion, were up $119 million, or 14.3 percent, from $1.603 billion in the same period last year, the OCEI figures showed.
Non-traditional exports fell $274 million, or 6.1 percent, to $4.213 billion in 1996.

"Common metals" was the strongest export sector in the first four months of 1997 with 36.9 percent of total exports. "Chemical products" came next with an 16.5 percent share, then "transport materials" with 8.2 percent.

The United States was the chief market for Venezuela's non- traditional exports with 25.9 percent. Venezuela's next largest export market was Colombia with a 25.4 percent share, followed by the Mexico with 3.7 percent, the Netherlands with 3.5 percent, Japan with 2.4 percent and the United Kingdom with 0.8 percent.
